cds.text: Understand that texts take many forms, such as signs, books and digital texts
Explore how texts are organised by purpose, such as to recount, narrate, express opinion, inform, report and explain
Identify how curriculum texts are organised differently and use language features depending on purpose
Understand conventions of print and screen, including how books and simple digital texts are organised
Explore how repetition, rhyme and rhythm create cohesion in simple poems, chants and songs
Understand how texts are made cohesive through personal and possessive pronouns and omitting inferable words
Understand how print and screen texts use features such as page numbers, contents, headings, titles, navigation buttons, links and images
Navigate print and screen texts using chapters, contents, indexes, side-bar or drop-down menus, and links
Create and take part in shared editing of short written texts to record and report ideas and events, using learnt vocabulary, basic punctuation and some CVC words spelled correctly

Create and re-read to edit short texts that report, express opinion or recount events, using simple grammatical sentences, topic vocabulary, end punctuation and some one- and two-syllable words spelled correctly

Create and edit short imaginative, informative and persuasive texts for familiar audiences, using purpose-appropriate structure, simple and compound sentences, noun and verb groups, and common two-syllable words
Create and deliver short spoken texts to report ideas and events to peers, using appropriate volume
Create and deliver short oral or multimodal presentations with an opening, middle and concluding statement, using topic vocabulary, gesture, volume and pace
Create, rehearse and deliver short presentations for familiar audiences, using purpose-appropriate structure, topic vocabulary, and varied tone, volume and pace
Form most lower-case and upper-case letters using learnt letter formations
Write words using unjoined lower-case and upper-case letters
Write words legibly, with growing fluency, using unjoined upper-case and lower-case letters
